counterfactual_missing_items: No caseating granulomas or acid-fast bacilli to support tuberculosis
No non-caseating granulomas to support sarcoidosis
No primary tumor identified to support metastatic cancer
decisive_items: Singular and large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes were noted in the neck and abdomen regions
response.rationale: C1 and R1 share identical raw support spans, but C1 provides a more complete label incorporating the specific pathological and anatomical findings. The biopsy showing proliferative heterotypic lymphoid cells is definitive for lymphoma, while other candidates rely on non-specific imaging findings or lack pathological confirmation.

rejected.why: Multiple lesions and bone destruction suggest metastasis, but the biopsy findings of proliferative lymphoid tissues are characteristic of lymphoma, not metastatic cancer.
Cavities and nodules may suggest tuberculosis, but no caseating granulomas or acid-fast bacilli are present; the pathological findings point to lymphoma.
Cavities and nodules could be sarcoidosis, but no non-caseating granulomas are seen; the biopsy is more consistent with lymphoma.
